seo.title: AI File Organizer — Organize Local Files With Preview and Approval
seo.description: Organize, rename, and sort local files with an AI agent that previews the proposed structure before making approved changes on your computer.

hero.title: Describe the order you want. Preview it before anything moves.
hero.description: Let Floatboat inspect a messy folder, propose a useful structure, and apply only the renames and moves you approve—directly on your computer.

demo.title: Inspect the proposed structure before applying it
demo.description: The organizer separates analysis from execution so you can correct categories and naming rules before files change.

features.title: More than moving files by extension.
features.description: Local file organization needs context beyond a filename. Explore how names, folder relationships, and document content inform proposed groups, while a preview gives you an opportunity to inspect changes before the approved file operations proceed.

useCases.title: Use Cases for AI File Organizer
useCases.description: Client folders, recurring records, and production assets need different filing rules. Compare how local organization can preserve project ownership, original locations, and relationships between files while leaving uncertain assignments for confirmation.

items.title: Separate client work cleanly
items.description: Incoming assets, contracts, and deliverables can be filed by client and project using the naming rules you provide. Keep uncertain assignments separate for confirmation instead of forcing every file into a category. Review the proposed structure before treating an ambiguous document as belonging to a particular client.

items.title: Standardize recurring records
items.description: Use approved filing rules to organize the current period's invoices, receipts, and reports. Standardize names and locations while recording where each item came from and what changed. A reviewable change list helps you check recurring records without losing the connection to their original files.

items.title: Tame footage and research
items.description: Production and research folders often contain related videos, transcripts, thumbnails, and drafts. Organize them by source and production stage so derived material remains connected to its original asset. When a filename does not establish the content or relationship, leave that assignment open rather than guessing.

comparison.title: Compare context-guided organization with fixed rules
comparison.description: The rule-only approach matches predefined conditions. Actual tools differ in preview, exception handling, and local execution; check those features separately.

items.question: Does organizing local files mean no data leaves my device?
items.answer: No. File operations can take place locally while selected content is sent to a model or connected service. Check the provider, tool permissions, and material involved before using sensitive files; a local folder alone is not a privacy guarantee.

items.question: Can it rename and move files together?
items.answer: Yes. A single approved plan can create folders, rename files, and move them into the proposed structure while reporting the result per file.

items.question: What happens when the agent is unsure?
items.answer: Uncertain matches should be surfaced for review rather than silently forced into a category. You can correct the plan before execution.

items.question: Can I reuse an organization system?
items.answer: Yes. A successful rule can become a reusable workflow for recurring exports, client onboarding, downloads, or project archives.

items.question: How should possible duplicate files be handled?
items.answer: Keep deletion out of the first organization pass. Review content, version history, and project references before deciding that two similar names identify the same file; retain uncertain candidates for a separate check.

items.question: How can I avoid breaking references when renaming a project folder?
items.answer: Start with a small copy or noncritical subset, identify documents and applications that refer to the old paths, and review proposed moves before applying them. A cleaner folder tree is not useful if it breaks links or working project files.

finalCta.title: Approve the folder plan before it changes files
finalCta.description: Point Floatboat at a messy folder, inspect proposed groups and renames, then apply only the moves you approve locally.

howTo.title: Organize files with a reviewed plan
howTo.description: A file-organizing task begins with a bounded directory and clear filing rules. Review the proposed structure before approving operations, then compare the actual changes and retained files with the preview rather than assuming every item was classified correctly.

items.title: Choose the folder and rules
items.description: Select the exact local folder, describe the target structure and naming rules, and mark folders that must stay unchanged.

items.title: Correct the proposed changes
items.description: Review classification, names, possible duplicates, and uncertain matches before approving any move or rename.

items.title: Approve and inspect the result
items.description: Authorize the reviewed operations, then inspect the move, rename, skip, and duplicate summary against the folder contents.
